display.purpose: Page headlines only, held to an 18ch measure.

figure.purpose: The single scored metric per screen. Gold, display scale.

body.purpose: All running copy at a 46-64ch measure.

label.purpose: Every field name. Defined once as label-caps so tracking cannot drift.

motion.name: ease-house
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out. Navigation slides and drawer entrances.

motion.name: dur-route
motion.purpose: Route cross-fade in the shell. The only entrance on a page load.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: useReducedMotion() is read in the shell and every duration above collapses. Non-negotiable: this is a tool opened many times a day.

components.name: Brand Button

narrative.overview:
A couture house's record book, not an analytics console. The account's growth is set the way a maison sets a lookbook: ivory stock, noir ink, one thread of antique gold, and enough silence around a figure that the figure means something. The measured numbers are the content — they are given display scale and a serif usually reserved for a magazine cover, because the whole product exists to make a small number of honest figures worth looking at.

The system's defining refusal is the container. There are no cards. Grouping is done with a 1px hairline and space, never with a filled, rounded, shadowed box. This is the single decision that separates this world from the dashboard it replaced.

The second refusal is decoration standing in for hierarchy. Emphasis comes from size, weight, and space — never from a tonal glow, a gradient, a coloured chip, or an icon beside a label.
keyCharacteristics: Ivory paper ground (#F7F4EE), never white, never dark
Bodoni Moda for display and every figure; Jost at weight 300 for everything else
One accent — antique gold — appearing perhaps twice per screen
Hairlines and space instead of cards, fills, and shadows
Near-square corners (1-2px), so nothing reads as a widget
Tabular figures everywhere, by default rather than per-component

rules.name: The Two Golds Rule
rules.body: #9C7C38 for large figures, #8A6B2C for anything a reader has to read at text size. One is 3.57:1 and one is 4.53:1, and the difference is whether the screen passes.

rules.name: The One Thread Rule
rules.body: Gold appears at most twice per screen. Its rarity is the entire effect; a third use makes it a theme colour and the maison becomes a brand guideline.

rules.name: The Ground Truth Rule
rules.body: Every data colour was validated against #F7F4EE. The previous set was validated against #0a0a0a. If the ground changes again, every chart colour is void until re-measured — a palette does not travel between grounds.

rules.name: The Didone Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Bodoni is for display and figures only. Below about 1.25rem it stops being elegant and starts costing legibility.

rules.name: The Tabular Default Rule
rules.body: Figures are tabular at the base layer, not per component. Numbers here are compared down columns, and a new component must not be able to ship proportional figures by omission.

rules.name: The Hairline-Only Rule
rules.body: If two regions need separating, the answer is a 1px #E0DACD rule and more space. Never a border-radius, never a fill, never a shadow, never a 2px accent border on one side.

rules.name: The Coarse Pointer Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element carries a 44px minimum target under @media (pointer: coarse), and only under it. The editorial rhythm depends on tight leading, so a mouse keeps the density and a thumb gets the target. The first build shipped 27px navigation items — elegant on a monitor, a miss on the phone where keywords actually get added.

rules.name: The Wayfinding Rule
rules.body: Every screen answers four questions: where am I, where can I go, what is here, and how do I leave. A screen that cannot answer all four is not finished, however well it is set.

rules.name: The Proximity Rule
rules.body: A control sits next to the thing it changes. A filter that governs one panel belongs to that panel, not to a toolbar at the top of the page.

dos: Do group with a 1px #E0DACD hairline and space.
Do use #8A6B2C for any gold a reader must read at text size, and reserve #9C7C38 for figures and headline accents.
Do set every measured number in Bodoni with tabular figures.
Do give one figure per screen the display scale and the gold; make the rest supporting.
Do carry counts alongside every rate, and render counts instead of a rate when the sample is thin.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion on every entrance and transition.
Do re-measure every data colour if the ground ever changes.
Do give every interactive element a 44px minimum target under a coarse pointer, and press feedback on pointer-down — hover does not exist on a phone.
Do check a finished screen against the four wayfinding questions before calling it done.
Do put a control beside the thing it governs.
donts: Don't put content in a card. No filled, bordered, rounded container as a page structure — this is the system's first rule.
Don't add a drop shadow anywhere.
Don't put an icon beside a navigation label, or introduce an icon set into the index.
Don't use gold as a data series colour, or a country colour as an accent.
Don't write an eyebrow or kicker above a heading, or number sections (01 / 02) when the order carries no information.
Don't give a coloured border to one side of a block; the hairline is uniform and 1px.
Don't animate each section in with the same staggered entrance. Motion is one authored moment per screen, not a template announcing itself.
Don't rely on hover to reveal anything a phone user needs. Eighty per cent of use is desktop; the other twenty per cent is where keywords get attached.
Don't import glass, backdrop blur, or a system font stack. This world was chosen against those, and they will arrive disguised as 'making it more Apple-like'.
